text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas says he did not know that the case against the chairman of the Lithuanian Savings Bank over alleged bribe-taking had been suspended.
- The president will discuss candidates for the post of prosecutor general with parliament's factions next week.
- The capitalisation of the stock exchange rose by 360 million litas last week to 6.532 billion litas.
- The biggest bank, the Lithuanian Agricultural Bank with 1.3 billion litas assets and 128 million litas share capital, forecast a 19.2 million loss in 1996.
- The deficit of the social security and pensions fund was 640.5 million litas in 1996.

- Parliament's national security comittee suggested that the head of the personnel department of the Ignalina nuclear power plant who issued job permits to five persons with mental problems be sacked.
- 85 percent of people still distrust commercial banks, an opinion poll showed. Lithuanians trusted the mass media, church and government most of all.

- If the elections took place tomorrow 23.9 percent of population would vote for the Homeland Union, 10.8 percent for the Centre Union, 8.4 percent for the Christian Democrats, 6.2 percent for the Social democrats and 5.9 percent for the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party.

- The government has suggested that the IMF freeze import tariffs for agricultural products at the present 27.5 percent level. The IMF memorandum requests that tarriffs be cut to 20 percent by March and to 10 percent by September.

- The management of Ignalina nuclear power does not meet international standards and it is becoming an obstacle on the country's path way to the European Union, parliament's national security comittee said.
- Russia's Gazprom threatened to reduce gas supply to Lithuania on February 1 if the country does not start to pay its debt of $41 million.
